newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Foreign strategy on Bosnia media flawed - report.
newsitem.headline: Foreign strategy on Bosnia media flawed - report.

text.p: International efforts to improve the independence of Bosnia's media have been largely ineffective despite millions of dollars in foreign assistance, a watchdog agency said on Saturday.
The International Crisis Group (ICG) said Bosnian media continue to fan the flames of ethnic hatred 15 months after the Dayton peace accord ended hostilities.
"Despite frenetic activity (by the international community), the media in Bosnia-Hercegovina remain divided into three separate and mutually antagonistic components," the ICG report explained.
Diplomats and outside observers blame biased local reporting for helping to foment the breakup of former Yugoslavia in 1991 and triggering the 43-month Bosnian war which followed.
The Dayton peace accord identified free and open media as a precondition to Bosnia building a peaceful, democratic society.
ICG charged that Bosnian media has not been reformed and that they are still reporting largely on the basis of separate Moslem, Serb and Croat viewpoints.

Under the Dayton accord the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) was charged with overseeing Bosnian elections and ensuring that local media created an environment for free and fair elections.
The OSCE persuaded leading state-run media to adopt its rules of conduct in the run-up to September 1996 national elections, but the agreed upon minimum standards were often violated.

With Bosnian municipal elections postponed until September of 1997, OSCE has a second chance to be more robust in dealing with media which are under the control of nationalist Moslem, Serb and Croat parties, ICG said.
An OSCE spokeswoman said the organisation was stepping up its efforts to try to minimise the ethnic-based reporting by local media. "We are trying to get them to report the facts," she said.
Foreign governments and agencies have contributed generously to the development of the independent media in Bosnia over the past five years, especially since the Dayton accord.

The ICG recommends that foreign donors research aid recipients prior to making awards to ensure that the money reaches non-nationalist media and supports long-term projects to train inexperienced journalists.
